title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: A contained spot-volatility reading meets a dense catalyst calendar, leaving equities especially sensitive to the jobs signal, long-end yields, AI-capex guidance and geopolitical oil risk.
volatilityRationale: The CBOE VIX was 15.95 at the Monday 11:00 UTC snapshot, a relatively contained spot reading, but markets are walking into multiple volatility channels: a packed AI-heavy earnings slate, ISM and labor data, the Treasury refunding announcement, elevated long-end yields and unresolved Middle East energy risk.

recap.text: The Federal Reserve held the federal-funds target range at 3.50%-3.75% on July 29 in a 9-3 vote; three members preferred a 25-basis-point hike, leaving policy uncertainty unusually visible despite the hold.
For the week ending July 31, SPY rose 1.07% and QQQ rose 0.86%, while IWM fell 0.58%, pointing to a firm large-cap finish but weaker small-cap breadth.
Mega-cap reactions split sharply: Microsoft and Amazon rallied on cloud and AI-demand strength, while Apple and Meta sold off on cautious guidance, higher spending or weaker cash-flow optics.
The long end of the Treasury curve remained a pressure point after the Fed hold, keeping duration-sensitive equities exposed even as stocks recovered into month-end.

Second-quarter GDP and June inflation data reinforced the cross-current: growth slowed while PCE inflation remained above target, leaving investors to balance recession risk against a still-hawkish policy backdrop.

triggers.text: U.S. ISM Manufacturing PMI and the first major AI read-through of the week via Palantir earnings; a softer activity signal or cautious AI guidance could pressure cyclicals and high-multiple software.
JOLTS job openings arrive alongside AMD, Arista Networks, Caterpillar and SpaceX earnings, creating a concentrated test of labor resilience, semiconductor demand and AI-infrastructure spending.
ADP employment and ISM Services are followed by earnings from SanDisk, Eli Lilly and Disney; the combination can move both growth expectations and real-economy defensives.
The U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding announcement is a potential duration and term-premium catalyst, particularly with long-end yields already elevated.

The July Employment Situation report is the week's highest-impact macro release; weak payrolls could revive easing hopes, while stronger hiring or wages could push yields and equity multiples in the opposite direction.

watch.text: Volatility gauge: the CBOE VIX was 15.95 at the Monday snapshot and closed the prior week at 15.99; a jump from this subdued base would confirm that the catalyst cluster is translating into realized risk. SKEW was not available in the current feed.

AI-capex breadth: compare Palantir, AMD, Arista and SpaceX commentary with the Microsoft and Amazon cloud-led rebound; confirmation of monetization would support the trade, while more spending-without-cash-flow warnings would reopen the valuation debate.
Labor and Fed sensitivity: watch payrolls, unemployment, wages and revisions together rather than the headline payroll number alone; the mix will shape the next rate-path repricing.
Oil and geopolitical risk: any renewed Iran or Strait of Hormuz disruption, or a surprise OPEC supply signal, could lift inflation expectations and add pressure to long-duration assets.
